cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Film genre is a categorisation system that groups films sharing similar narrative patterns, visual styles, themes and emotional effects.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Steve Neale argued that genre depends on both repetition of conventions and difference and variation to sustain audience interest.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: The 'repertoire of elements' describes the set of conventions that characterise a genre — setting, character types, iconography, narratives and themes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Iconography refers to the visual symbols and recurring images associated with a genre: cowboy hats in westerns, spaceships in sci-fi, masks in horror.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Audience expectations are shaped by genre knowledge — viewers anticipate certain experiences and pleasures based on the genre they have chosen.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Genre conventions are not fixed rules but shared expectations between filmmakers and audiences that can be fulfilled or subverted.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Genre cycles describe how genres evolve over time: from establishment through classic phases to parody, revisionism and potential revival.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Rick Altman proposed that genres operate on two levels: as semantic systems of shared conventions and as syntactic systems of recurring narrative structures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Hybrid genres emerge when conventions from two or more genres combine, creating fresh experiences that attract wider or different audiences.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Institutional contexts shape genre production: studios develop genre formulas based on commercial viability and audience demand.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Genre serves an industrial function: studios use genre to market films and audiences use genre to make viewing choices.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Genre Theory & Conventions
cards.back: Understanding genre is essential for film analysis because it provides a framework of expectations against which individual films can be read.
